Solving one- and two-vertex moment equations yields the exact mean and variance. The normalized part-fraction difference satisfies a coercive drift and a vanishing stationarity quadratic-variation bound. Taylor expansion of the slow sum fraction after N scaling identifies all limit polynomial moments with Beta(2theta,2(1-theta)), and compact moment determinacy completes the joint law. From packaged verification source, 25 exact-rational finite-generator comparisons and 55 algebraic moment recursions passed; experiments are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A canonical voter system with only one fixed positive and one fixed negative agent has a nonconcentrating continuum of stationary macrostates. The precisely evaluated partition-dependent variance has sharp fixed-network-size maximizers and a remarkable balanced-class uniform weak limit. The beta shape for imbalanced communities is a complete natural probability-law classification, not merely a reproduced covariance recipe or textbook formula.
